In Comanche we don’t really have something that translates exactly to hello or goodbye.
There are a couple of commands that will work. 
Marʉawe (Report/tell it!) for a greeting. 
Tsaaku mia (go in a good way!) for a farewell. 
Both of these phrases are the way you would say it to o ly one person.

a94f316fe027.category: African Americans in World War II
a94f316fe027.credit: Archive of the Desmond-Fish Public Library, Fish family collection
a94f316fe027.description: This is a photograph of the 15th Regiment New York Infantry, at Camp Whitman, near Poughkeepsie, New York. It was the only Black National Guard regiment in New York State. Commanded by Colonel William Hayward, it was commissioned to Federal service on July 25, 1917, becoming the 369th Infantry Regiment, later to be known as the "Harlem Hellfighters" for their celebrated bravery.
